summary.headline: Global Surfaces Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% to Rs 65 crore and EBITDA turned to Rs 8 crore, with PAT at break-even, despite 27% utilisation.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 65 crore (up 44%), EBITDA of Rs 8 crore versus a Rs 19 crore loss in the prior quarter (margin 12.69%), and PAT break-even versus a Rs 2 crore loss. Overall capacity utilisation was about 27% (Dubai 20%, India 36%), held back by shipping disruption via Hormuz in March–April. The Bagru natural stone unit was discontinued from March 31, 2026 and is being wound down, with asset disposal targeted within FY27. Management declined to give FY27 revenue or utilisation guidance, citing US tariff and geopolitical uncertainty, including a US ITC safeguard recommendation on quartz surfaces.

financial_highlights.change: +44% (as stated on call; an analyst's question cited a 12% YoY decline, which was not addressed directly)
vs EBITDA loss of Rs 19 crore in previous quarter

management later cited 28% as of the call date

segments.name: Dubai (Global Surfaces FZE, Jebel Ali)
segments.commentary: Q1 utilisation 20%, and FY26 revenue was about Rs 160 crore at 44% utilisation. Management said the unit was EBITDA positive in June 2026 and in FY26.

segments.name: India (Jaipur)
segments.commentary: Q1 utilisation 36%. FY26 revenue was about Rs 72 crore (Rs 232 crore total less Dubai's Rs 160 crore). Domestic revenue is described as insignificant so far.

segments.name: Bagru natural stone unit
segments.commentary: Discontinued from March 31, 2026. FY26 loss was about Rs 7–8 crore on revenue of about Rs 12–14 crore. Board has appointed a valuer and management expects disposal within FY27; no sale value has been set.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 revenue, volume or utilisation guidance; management said the worst is done and expects improvement once geopolitics stabilise.
Management said break-even was reached at about 28–30% utilisation, and profitability should scale sharply once utilisation improves.
Freight costs in UAE have not normalised from Q1 levels; about 30–40% of the cost increase has been passed on to customers.
India domestic launch in Q2 FY27 via a dealer/distributor model; sales team to grow from about 9–10 to 25–30 people over the next quarter, with about 15 added in India.

Management expects a substantial domestic revenue contribution over the next few financial years but gave no figure; a marketing budget has been set internally for the next two quarters, amount not disclosed.
Peak revenue split between Dubai and India is roughly 65:35, described as a ballpark figure.
capex_capacity: Combined annual capacity is 1.14 million sq m (about 11.5 lakh sq m per analyst's question, which management did not contest).
Overall utilisation was 27% in Q1 and 28% as of the call date; utilisation was affected by shipping constraints.
Shipping from Dubai moved to alternative ports (Sohar, Khor Fakkan, Fujairah) and resumed in May–June 2026.
Bagru unit: production stopped March 31, 2026; finishing backlog lots, disposing of finished stock, and seeking a buyer for the property.
Marquartz Technology (patented, one of only two global manufacturers) launched; it is cited as driving Dubai product mix.
demand_pricing: US tariffs: 50% effective in Aug 2025 (25% reciprocal plus 25% Russia-linked); interim framework in Feb 2026 cut reciprocal tariff to 18% and removed the Russia-linked tariff.

US ITC found quartz surface imports a substantial cause of serious injury under Section 201 (petition April 2026); recommended a four-year TRQ with 25% in-quota and 50% above-quota tariff in year one. Final measures pending.
Management said there has been no major change in product demand, and the order book is strong.
Freight/trade costs rose to nearly twice normal levels; resin-linked raw material costs rose in India and the Middle East.
Diversification: GCC (UAE focus), European markets (sales team deployed, results awaited), and India. Named domestic peers: Asian, Classic Marble and Spectrum.
Most US clients are distributors (including big-box retailers and fabricators); no residential/commercial split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Dubai utilisation, US shipping and tariff hurdles, and the raw material cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Dubai utilisation was 20% and India 36% in Q1, because of shipping disruption in March–April. Raw material costs rose globally with freight and resin; some costs were passed on, and management expects stability once geopolitics settles.

qa_highlights.question: Planned India domestic model and marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Distributors will be appointed in major cities, selling to B2C end customers under the Global Surfaces brand. A marketing budget is set for the next two quarters but the amount was not disclosed; some international fairs were dropped to offset cost.

qa_highlights.question: Margin aspiration once utilisation improves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said break-even was reached at about 28–30% utilisation and profitability should scale significantly once utilisation rises, subject to geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: Dubai revenue and peak revenue split between facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Dubai revenue was about Rs 160 crore in FY26 at 44% utilisation. Peak split across Dubai and India is roughly 65:35, described as a ballpark figure.

qa_highlights.question: Freight normalisation and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: UAE freight has not normalised from Q1 levels. About 30–40% of the cost increase has been passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Bagru asset disposal timing and cash proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: A valuer has been appointed and buyers are being approached; no number has been set. Management expects disposal within FY27.

risks_watch: US Section 201 final quartz safeguard measures (TRQ, 25%/50% tariffs) and the possibility of exemptions.
Persistent Hormuz/Middle East shipping disruption and elevated UAE freight; only 30–40% of cost increases passed on so far.
Low utilisation (20% Dubai, 36% India) and dependence on the recovery in volumes for margin sustainability.
Execution risk and marketing burn in the India launch scheduled for Q2 FY27 (sales team scaling from 9–10 to 25–30 people).
Bagru disposal value and timing; no sale price has been identified.
Clarity on the Q1 revenue growth basis: the company said +44%, but an analyst's question cited a 12% YoY decline. Verify against the filed results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on cost discipline and the margin turn, but evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 revenue, utilisation or peak revenue guidance, citing geopolitical and tariff uncertainty. Answers were sometimes vague or inconsistent, for example on marketing spend and the Dubai/India split.
